Folks — I reviewed ACME's redline and put together three negotiation paths with sample clause text and practical notes. Quick summary up front: recommend Option B (compromise) for enterprise procurement customers of this size unless they commit to security controls and insurance proof.

Option A — Conservative (legal-preferred): keep a single overall cap tied to fees; limited carve-out for gross negligence only.
Sample clause (short):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the aggregate liability of Redwood for any and all claims arising out of or in connection with this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (i) $1,000,000 or (ii) the total Fees paid by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. The foregoing cap shall not apply to liability resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct."
Practical: minimizes exposure; will be a difficult sell if customer insists on data-loss carve-outs.

Option B — Compromise (recommended): keep a single overall cap but carve out a capped data-loss bucket and define a per-incident subcap for catastrophic data incidents. This balances commercial risk and customer concern.
Sample clause (short):
"Except for liability resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct, Customer's aggregate recovery for all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall be limited to the greater of (i) $1,000,000 or (ii) three (3) times the Fees paid by Customer in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim. Notwithstanding the foregoing, for claims arising from unauthorized access to or loss of Customer Data, Redwood's liability shall be limited to $5,000,000 per incident and $10,000,000 in the aggregate. Liability for lost profits shall be limited to $500,000 per incident and shall not be recoverable as consequential damages except in cases of gross negligence or willful misconduct."
Practical: gives ACME a meaningful remedy for data incidents while keeping our absolute exposure capped. Use this if ACME is sensitive but insurance backstops are available.

Option C — Commercial (sales-oriented): higher caps and broader carve-outs in exchange for contractual commitments (PCI/Pen tests/SOC 2 attestation/insurance).
Sample clause (short):
"Customer's aggregate liability shall be limited to $10,000,000 per occurrence and $20,000,000 in aggregate. For data incidents, Redwood shall be liable for reasonable third-party costs, notification and remediation up to $10,000,000 per incident. Lost profits shall be recoverable up to $2,000,000 where Customer can provide reasonable documentation of loss and subject to prior notice and mitigation obligations."
Practical: Only justify for strategic customers that bring material ARR and can provide coverage (cyber insurance). High commercial cost.

Negotiation playbook (one-liners to use on call):
- "We can narrow carve-outs to authenticated data exposure that materially impacts production systems; we won't agree to unlimited liability for general business losses."
- "If you'd like broader remedies, we can trade that for insurance confirmation and a higher per-incident cap in the order form."
- "We prefer per-incident subcaps because they limit tail risk and are easier to re-insure."

Draft redline and two order form variants attached in my notes (I can produce the .docx if helpful). If we go with Option B, I'll draft the redline language for both MSA and order form with fallback markers.

Anna — thanks for the candid redline and for highlighting ACME's priorities. We want to keep the deal moving and have discussed internally. Below is a concise counterproposal and the path we recommend.

Summary counterproposal (Order Form-level commercial solution):
- Maintain a clear overall cap tied to fees: greater of $1,000,000 or three (3) times the annual fees (12 months preceding claim). This preserves predictability for both parties.
- Carve-out bucket for "Data Incidents": per-incident subcap of $5,000,000 and $10,000,000 aggregate for unauthorized access to or loss of Customer Data (defined narrowly as production customer data as set out in the Data Appendix).
- Lost profits (consequential damages): recoverable only up to $500,000 per incident and $1,000,000 aggregate, except where liability arises from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
- Reasonable third-party notification, credit monitoring and remediation costs: recoverable up to the Data Incident subcap.

Rationale: this gives ACME meaningful recovery for material data incidents while keeping Redwood's exposure bounded. We are willing to expand the Data Incident subcap if ACME provides evidence of cyber insurance with a defined minimum coverage and includes Redwood as a named insured/endorsement.

Next steps:
1) If ACME is comfortable with the above, we will circulate a redline for the MSA and an Order Form addendum reflecting the per-incident subcap and insurance commitment language.
2) If ACME prefers no cap for data incidents, please confirm the specific commercial consideration you are seeking (higher fees / longer term / insurance) so we can evaluate.
3) Recommend a 30-minute sync to finalize — I'm available Wed/Thu afternoon PT.
